fullPassage:
According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is natural happiness, and we experience it when we do get what we want. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value. Choosing synthetic happiness produces comparable positive outcomes, health advantages, and a similar sense of well-being.
For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you.
Surround yourself with people who inspire you and embrace you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life, and, most importantly, those who make your day brighter.
Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to value these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness. Without valuing what you already have, it's challenging to express thankfulness for anything else.
Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that enhance your overall happiness levels.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called (A)[synthetic / sympathetic] happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is (B)[natural / neutral] happiness, and we experience it when we do get what we want. In our society, we hold the (C)[belief / relief] that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 첫 번째는 인위적 행복, 두 번째는 자연적 행복. 우리 사회는 자연적 행복이 우월하다는 믿음을 갖고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) synthetic: '인위적 행복'. sympathetic(동정적인)은 의미 다름. ✅ (B) natural: '자연적 행복'. neutral(중립적)은 의미 다름. ✅ (C) belief: '믿음'. relief(안도)는 의미 다름.
det.tip: synthetic(인위적) vs sympathetic(동정적). natural(자연적) vs neutral(중립적). belief(믿음) vs relief(안도).

questions.passage: Surround yourself with people who (A)[inspire / expire] you and embrace you. Healthy and (B)[meaningful / meaningless] friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely (C)[admire / ignore], those who bring positivity into your life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 당신에게 영감을 주고 포용하는 사람들로 둘러싸라. 의미 있는 우정은 상호 지지 위에 세워진다. 진정으로 존경하는 친구를 선택하라.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) inspire: '영감을 주다'. expire(만료되다)는 의미 다름. ✅ (B) meaningful: '의미 있는'. meaningless(무의미한)는 반대. ✅ (C) admire: '존경하다'. ignore(무시하다)는 반대.
det.tip: inspire(영감을 주다) vs expire(만료되다). meaningful(의미있는) ↔ meaningless(무의미한).

questions.passage: Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal (A)[significance / ignorance] and lasting value. Choosing synthetic happiness produces (B)[comparable / incompatible] positive outcomes, health advantages, and a similar sense of (C)[well-being / well-known].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인위적 행복은 동등한 중요성과 지속적 가치를 지닌다. 비슷한 긍정적 결과와 안녕감을 준다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) significance: '중요성'. ignorance(무지)는 반대. ✅ (B) comparable: '비슷한'. incompatible(양립불가)은 반대. ✅ (C) well-being: '안녕감'. well-known(유명한)은 의미 다름.
det.tip: significance(중요성) vs ignorance(무지). comparable(비슷한) vs incompatible(양립불가).

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a ①<u>precious</u> moment of happiness. The ②<u>power</u> to choose happiness lies within you. Surround yourself with people who inspire you and ③<u>embrace</u> you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on ④<u>competitive</u> support for each other's happiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 건강하고 의미 있는 우정은 서로의 행복에 대한 상호(mutual) 지지 위에 세워진다. competitive(경쟁적)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①precious: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②power: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③embrace: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④competitive: 원문은 mutual. 우정은 경쟁이 아닌 상호 지지.
det.tip: mutual(상호적) ↔ competitive(경쟁적). 우정의 기반은 상호 지지.

questions.passage: Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. When you ①<u>appreciate</u> what's already in your life, you begin to ②<u>value</u> these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness. Without valuing what you already have, it's ③<u>challenging</u> to express ④<u>resentment</u> for anything else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이미 가진 것에 가치를 두지 않으면 다른 것에 감사(thankfulness)를 표현하기 어렵다. resentment(원망)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①appreciate: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②value: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③challenging: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④resentment: 원문은 thankfulness. 감사가 아닌 원망은 문맥 반대.
det.tip: thankfulness(감사) ↔ resentment(원망, 분개). 감사를 표현해야 하는 맥락.

questions.passage: Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends ①<u>signals</u> to the brain that there is ②<u>cause</u> to be happy and satisfied. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that ③<u>diminish</u> your overall happiness ④<u>levels</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뇌가 '기분 좋은' 화학물질을 방출하여 전반적인 행복 수준을 향상(enhance)시킨다. diminish(줄이다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①signals: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②cause: 원문 그대로. ❌ ③diminish: 원문은 enhance. 행복을 줄이는 것이 아니라 높이는 것. ✅ ④levels: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: enhance(향상시키다) ↔ diminish(줄이다). feel-good chemicals는 행복을 높이는 역할.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is natural happiness, and we experience it when we do get what we want. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is __________ to synthetic happiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리 사회는 자연적 행복이 인위적 행복보다 우월하다고 믿는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④superior: 'superior to ~'는 '~보다 우월한'. ❌ ①inferior(열등한): 반대. ❌ ②identical(동일한): 다른 의미. ❌ ③irrelevant(무관한): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: superior to(~보다 우월한) ↔ inferior to(~보다 열등한).

questions.passage: Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to value these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness. Without valuing what you already have, it's challenging to express __________ for anything else.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이미 가진 것에 가치를 두지 않으면 다른 것에 감사를 표현하기 어렵다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①thankfulness: 가치 인식 → 감사 표현의 맥락. ❌ ②curiosity(호기심): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ③ambition(야망): 무관. ❌ ④sympathy(동정): 무관.
det.tip: thankfulness(감사): appreciate(감사하다) → value(가치를 두다) → thankfulness(감사)의 논리적 흐름.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is natural happiness. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Dr. Gilbert suggests that synthetic happiness is __________ natural happiness in terms of its value and significance.

det.korean: 길버트 박사는 인위적 행복이 가치와 중요성 면에서 자연적 행복과 동등하게 가치 있다고 제안한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③just as valuable as: 'holds equal significance and lasting value'와 일치. ❌ ①far superior(훨씬 우월): 과장. ❌ ②completely different(완전히 다른): 가치는 같다고 함. ❌ ④much less important(훨씬 덜 중요): 반대.
det.tip: equal significance = just as valuable. 인위적 행복의 가치를 재평가하는 글.

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a <u>precious</u> moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'precious'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 불행을 느끼는 매 순간마다 소중한 행복의 순간을 잃는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②valuable: precious(소중한)와 동의어. ❌ ①ordinary(평범한): 반대. ❌ ③brief(짧은): 다른 의미. ❌ ④frequent(잦은): 무관.
det.tip: precious ≈ valuable: 소중한, 귀중한.

questions.passage: Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that <u>enhance</u> your overall happiness levels.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'enhance'와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 뇌가 전반적 행복 수준을 향상시키는 화학물질을 방출한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③improve: enhance(향상시키다)와 동의어. ❌ ①reduce(줄이다): 반대. ❌ ②maintain(유지하다): 다른 의미. ❌ ④measure(측정하다): 무관.
det.tip: enhance ≈ improve: 향상시키다, 높이다.

questions.passage: Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you <u>genuinely</u> admire, those who bring positivity into your life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'genuinely'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 진정으로 존경하는 친구를 선택하라. genuinely(진심으로)의 반의어.
det.analysis: ✅ ④insincerely: genuinely(진심으로)의 반의어 '불성실하게'. ❌ ①truly(진정으로): 동의어. ❌ ②sincerely(진심으로): 동의어. ❌ ③honestly(정직하게): 동의어.
det.tip: genuinely(진심으로) ↔ insincerely(불성실하게). truly, sincerely, honestly는 모두 유사어.

questions.passage: In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is <u>superior</u> to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'superior'와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 자연적 행복이 인위적 행복보다 우월하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①inferior: superior(우월한)의 반의어 '열등한'. ❌ ②equivalent(동등한): 반의어 아님. ❌ ③comparable(비슷한): 반의어 아님. ❌ ④dominant(지배적인): 유사어.
det.tip: superior(우월한) ↔ inferior(열등한). superior to ↔ inferior to.

questions.passage:
(A) Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting <u>value</u>.

(B) When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to <u>value</u> these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 'value'와 (B)의 'value'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 지속적인 가치. (B) 이것들을 더 소중히 여기기 시작한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A)value=가치(명사): lasting value. (B)value=소중히 여기다(동사): begin to value. ❌ ① 가격은 문맥 불일치. ❌ ③ 계산하다는 의미 다름. ❌ ④ 가격은 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: value: ①가치(명사) ②소중히 여기다(동사) ③가격(명사). 품사와 맥락으로 구분.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"not naturally produced; artificially created or manufactured"

det.korean: "자연적으로 생산되지 않은; 인위적으로 만들어진"
det.analysis: ✅ ③synthetic: 인위적인, 합성의. 정의와 일치. ❌ ①natural(자연적): 반대. ❌ ②neutral(중립적): 다른 개념. ❌ ④sympathetic(동정적): 다른 개념.
det.tip: synthetic(합성의, 인위적인): 본문에서 'synthetic happiness(인위적 행복)'. artificial과 동의어.

questions.passage: Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

She received great __________ (admire) from her colleagues for her dedication to the project.

det.korean: 그녀는 프로젝트에 대한 헌신으로 동료들로부터 큰 존경을 받았다.
det.analysis: ✅ admiration: great + __________ → 명사. admire(동사) → admiration(명사).
det.tip: admire(존경하다, 동사) → admiration(존경, 명사). -ation 접미사로 명사 형성.

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The children felt __________ (happiness) when they received their gifts.

det.korean: 아이들은 선물을 받았을 때 행복하게 느꼈다.
det.analysis: ✅ happy: felt + __________ → 형용사(보어). happiness(명사) → happy(형용사).
det.tip: happiness(행복, 명사) → happy(행복한, 형용사). feel + 형용사(감각동사 + 보어).

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you. Surround yourself with people who inspire you and embrace you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life, and, most importantly, those who make your day __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 당신의 하루를 더 밝게 만드는 친구를 선택하라.
det.analysis: ✅ ②brighter: '하루를 밝게 하다'는 긍정적 영향. ❌ ①shorter(짧게): 부정적. ❌ ③simpler(단순하게): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④quieter(조용하게): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: make your day brighter: 하루를 밝게 하다. 긍정적 영향을 주는 친구.

questions.passage: Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value. Choosing synthetic happiness produces <u>comparable</u> positive outcomes, health advantages, and a similar sense of well-being.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'comparable'과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 인위적 행복은 비슷한 긍정적 결과를 만든다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③similar: comparable(비슷한, 비교할 만한)과 동의어. ❌ ①incompatible(양립불가): 반대. ❌ ②competitive(경쟁적): 다른 의미. ❌ ④superior(우월한): 다른 의미.
det.tip: comparable ≈ similar: 비슷한, 비교할 만한. equal과도 유사.

questions.passage: Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value. Choosing synthetic happiness produces comparable positive outcomes, health advantages, and a similar sense of well-being.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The research findings are __________ (significance) because they change our understanding of happiness.

det.korean: 연구 결과가 중요하다. be + 형용사.
det.analysis: ✅ significant: are + __________ → 형용사(보어). significance(명사) → significant(형용사).
det.tip: significance(중요성, 명사) → significant(중요한, 형용사). be + 형용사.
